blocked.reason: No public machine interface. Both probed URLs returned HTML ASP.NET portal pages (trialsearch.who.int), not queryable records; scraping the portal is out of scope. Primary registries (CT.gov, CTIS) are collected directly instead.

Documented awards API (no key required) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every request, including a browser-style fetch, while the official https://www.sbir.gov/api page carried a maintenance notice on 2026-11-09. Not a registration requirement; recorded UNAVAILABLE with evidence so a later re-probe can retry.

cross_entity_links.paper_to_grant: implemented and unit-tested (Crossref funder[].award[] / Europe PMC grantId / OpenAlex award ids matched against grant award ids after normalisation); live match rate not asserted because the sweep did not include grant records
cross_entity_links.paper_to_trial: implemented and unit-tested on structurally published NCT ids only; the sampled Europe PMC records exposed no NCT cross-references, so the live link rate was 0 in this batch and is reported as 0 rather than estimated

company_links.rule: only structured source fields count; reported as separate tiers: funder, author_affiliation, lead_sponsor, collaborator, grantee, participant; text mentions are never counted

connector_coverage_note: The lead asked for connectors on openalex / europepmc / crossref / clinicaltrials_gov / nih_reporter first; those five plus pubmed_eutils (needed for the cross-source duplicate measurement) ship. semantic_scholar, openaire, eu_ctis, eu_cordis are verified but probe-only: no connector, per the lead's priority. who_ictrp and sbir_gov could not be verified and correctly ship no connector.

doi_positive_control.design: three known DOIs looked up in each source's native identifier form
doi_positive_control.interpretation: For the same work, the four sources yield four records that collapse to one: a naive count would over-state scholarly evidence by 4x. This is why every count in this handoff is a unique-work count, never a raw-row count.

five_firm_sweep.interpretation: At fixed depth 25 the four engines' relevance rankings are largely disjoint for a broad company-name query, so duplication is low (0-9%). The engines are therefore complementary rather than redundant for firm sweeps.

dedupe.rule: publication identifiers only (DOI > PMID > PMCID), identifier-union clustering; records sharing ANY of the three are one work; records with no publication identifier remain singletons and are counted separately

notable_findings: EU CTIS exposes an unauthenticated JSON API at https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public-api (POST /search, GET /retrieve/{ctNumber}); it returns real trial records including publishDate, decisionDateOverall, startDateEU and sponsor, which unlocks the EU trial lane that CT.gov cannot see.

CORDIS has no official developer API, but the public site's unauthenticated JSON endpoints work: /search/en?format=json returns 'result' reports only, while /project/id/{id}?format=json returns real project factsheets (startDate, endDate, ecSignatureDate, ecMaxContribution, participant organisations) — so grants are retrievable in a two-step search-then-resolve pattern.

Same work, four sources: exact-DOI lookups returned 4 records collapsing to 1 unique work (75% duplicate ratio), so a naive multi-source count over-states scholarly evidence by up to 4x; every figure reported here is a de-duplicated unique-work count.

Broad firm sweeps are complementary, not redundant: at depth 25 the four engines' result sets overlapped 0-9% (Medtronic 0%, Mindray 9%), so cross-source collection adds recall for company sweeps and the de-duplicator mostly matters for topic/DOI-anchored collection.

Crossref funder metadata is the strongest paper-to-company hook: 21 of the top-25 'Medtronic' Crossref hits were works funded by Medtronic (tier 'funder'), while Europe PMC supplied author-affiliation and grant-agency hits and OpenAlex supplied ROR-linked author affiliations.

PubMed esummary carries neither author affiliations nor funder award ids, so PubMed alone can never attribute a paper to a firm; company attribution must come from Europe PMC core, OpenAlex or Crossref. This is recorded in the PubMed connector docstring and the source register instead of being patched over.

OpenAlex's created_date is frequently years after publication_date (sample: publication 2012-01-31, created 2016-06-24), which is exactly the look-ahead hazard the protocol forbids — the connectors preserve created_date/deposited/firstIndexDate only as metadata_clock_fields and never use them as the public clock.
open_questions: CTIS publishDate semantics: the retrieved sample had decisionDate 2023-10 but publishDate 2026-09, so publishDate may be a record-publication/update timestamp rather than first public visibility. Validating this against trial events needs a larger CTIS sample.

CORDIS fielded-query syntax is undocumented and fails silently ('contenttype=project' as a query returned an empty hit set; a numeric query returned HTTP 500). A reliable project-typed search would avoid the two-step resolve and is still unresolved.

Live paper-to-trial link rate: no structurally published NCT ids appeared in the sampled Europe PMC records, so the linkage implementation is tested only on synthetic records. A targeted sample of device-trial publications is needed to measure it.
Whether OpenAlex awards/funders coverage is dense enough for industrial device literature; the sampled Medtronic-affiliated work carried empty funders/awards.
